I work with people in disability. The payments vary wildly. If you are disabled and get disability before age 24 I think, it is based partially on your parents income.

If you are disabled and paid into the system, it would be around $1200 monthly. This allows you to get food stamps and section 8 housing or whatever your states low income housing is. You then pay up to one third of your payment for rent. You get discounted electric or gas for heating and cooling. You also qualify for state health insurance and Medicaid.

In total, you get a shot ton of benefits equal to $2400 a month in my area since rent is so high. I have people paying $290 for apartments that cost their neighbors $1500 .

If I had to guess, I would say the average SSDI payment is around $1150 a month of you paid into it and had enough credits for the full amount. If they never worked, I would say it is about $880 monthly. Keep in mind the health benefits. No copays and $1 prescriptions on most things.

Edit: My estimate or $2400 in value per month in benefits does not factor in the value of the medical plan so it is much higher.

I know you were asking about the US but I thought you may be interested in the UK benefits too. I suffer with severe mental health problems that affect me so much I struggle with daily life, I am an unwell woman. I have been mentally ill since I was 13 and when I came out of hospital (psychiatric ward) I was told to sign a form by my Mam, I did and I have had benefits ever since, although I have gone through the severe stress of them stopping during assessment. Here in the UK the two benefits for disabled people like myself is called ESA (Employment and Support allowance) and PIP (personal independence payment) , ESA is the general "I can't work due to illness/injury benefit" while PIP is for disabled people only. ESA splits you into two groups, one who need to engage with job related activities and one where you don't have to do any work or look for it, I am in the second group. I receive both and get about £650 a month to live on, because I sort of own the house I live in, I contribute £100 to the mortgage (my fiancé does too) and my bills cost £190 ish. If I was renting I would be claiming housing benefit, instead my local council has made me exempt from paying council tax at all (saving over £100 a month). I also have been given a bus pass that allows me and my fiancé (my full time carer as well) free bus travel and train discount all over Wales which has helped massively. Before most of our money was going to paying for travel (£4 .00 minimum each) to appointments and doctors and we were hardly able to afford to go anywhere, it's helped me to try and get out more and to face my anxieties to try and get better. I don't get any discounts on my bills but thanks to the other things I have, the cost isn't so hard to keep up with.

I am also eligible for a disabled train pass, discounts at attractions, museums ect. I have a card that allows me a free carer ticket to performances in a network of Welsh theatres (including one of the biggest, the Wales Millenium Centre) and a ticket to allow a free carer at any national trust property.

I have also found that the fact I need to keep my meds with me and other similar things useful, for instance, when I was boarding the plane from Vienna to the UK the crew were putting people's cabin bags in the hold, I got to keep mine because of my medications, I cannot risk losing them. .

Without the help I receive i would not be able to be independent which is something I highly value, my independence is so important to me and it's a miracle I am able to live in my own place and sustain it, my fiancé is my hero. I wish I was not reliant on the system and I feel bad for being on benefits but I really am not well enough mentally to cope and live with normal things, like going to a shop, i wish this was different because I wanted a big career in travel but the cold reality is that I will never have it because of my mental illness, which I will most likely gave for life despite round after round of different therapies. I am hoping to start voluntary work to try and help me get out and be with people more among other things, if I can't work I would at least like to support my local community and give back as much as I can, at the moment I could do 2-3 hours a week but I hope to build on that.

Recent,y they have been very strict with PIP and many people have had their PIP stopped, I imagine a lot of fats had it stopped so that's a bonus!

Hope that was interesting for you!
